findings.title: Backup code login can skip the password
findings.body: The new backup-code branch in credentials authorize never checks the password. Password verification only runs when `credentials.totpCode` is empty (`if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)` above this branch). A request that includes any non-empty `totpCode` (it does not have to be a valid authenticator code) plus a valid `backupCode` therefore skips both the password check and the TOTP check and is logged in. The same `totpCode` flag also bypasses the non-CAL identity-provider rejection. Backup codes are long-lived secrets users download as a text file; with this hole, that file alone is enough for account takeover, including for accounts that were later linked to Google/SAML. The branch must verify the password (for any user that has one) itself, and must not treat a dummy `totpCode` as proof of the first factor.

findings.title: Backup code consumption is not atomic
findings.body: After a matching backup code is found, the handler sets that slot to null and writes the whole encrypted list back with a plain `user.update`. Two concurrent authorize calls can both read the same ciphertext, both observe the code as unused, and both return a successful login. If the requests use two different codes, the later write restores the code the earlier request already consumed, so a one-time code stays valid. Disable can race the same way: a login that read the user before disable completes will write `backupCodes` back after disable nulled them. Consume the code with a conditional update (transaction/`SELECT FOR UPDATE`, or update only where the stored ciphertext is still the value that was read) and retry or fail if the row changed.

findings.title: Backup code match is case-sensitive and not trimmed
findings.body: Stored codes are lowercase hex from `randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`, but login accepts a code only after `replaceAll("-", "")` and a strict `indexOf`. The entry placeholder is `XXXXX-XXXXX`, and people commonly type or transcribe backup codes in uppercase or with spaces. Those inputs fail the match and the user is told the code is incorrect even though it is one of the codes they were shown. The same comparison is copied in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` at the `indexOf` on the submitted backup code, so disabling 2FA with a backup code has the same false rejection. Normalize by lowercasing and stripping every non-hex character before comparing.

findings.title: Backup codes can be dismissed forever after 2FA is already on
findings.body: 2FA is enabled on the server before the backup-code step is shown, and the plaintext codes exist only in this modal's state. `onEnable` (which is what the parent uses to refresh the switch and close the flow) runs only from the Close button. `onOpenChange` is passed straight through to `Dialog` and is not blocked on this step, and Cancel is hidden here, so Escape, overlay click, or the dialog close control dismisses the only view of the codes without calling `onEnable`. There is no later screen to reveal or regenerate codes (existing users with a null `backupCodes` column are told to generate them in settings, which this PR does not add). The user can end up with 2FA on, a settings switch still showing off, and no saved backup codes. Keep the dialog from closing until the user confirms they stored the codes, and call the same completion path as Close.

findings.title: Copy reports success even when clipboard write fails
findings.body: `navigator.clipboard.writeText` is not awaited and has no `.catch`, but `showToast(..., "success")` runs immediately. If the clipboard API rejects (permissions policy, insecure context, denied prompt), the user still sees "Backup codes copied!" and an unhandled rejection is thrown. Because this screen is the only time the codes are shown, a false success followed by Close leaves them with no codes. Await the write and show the success toast only after it resolves; surface a failure toast otherwise.

findings.title: Tests never log in or disable 2FA with a backup code
findings.body: The new coverage only clicks download, copy, and close on the setup dialog. Download checks the filename but not the file contents, and copy only waits for the success toast, which is shown even when `clipboard.writeText` fails, so a broken copy still passes. Nothing submits a backup code to credentials authorize or to `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable`, which is the path that can skip the password and that burns codes. The other enable test in this file was not updated to dismiss the new backup-code step at all, and its switch assertion is the one the new comment says passes even when the switch is unchecked, so CI will not catch a setup flow that never finishes. Add a login (and disable) that uses a code from the encrypted `backupCodes` column, including a second use of the same code that must fail.

findings.title: Missing-backup-codes message points at a flow that does not exist
findings.body: `missing_backup_codes` tells the user "Please generate them in your settings." This PR never adds a regenerate action. Users who enabled 2FA before the migration have `backupCodes` null, and the only way to get codes is to disable 2FA with the authenticator and set it up again. Lost-access login and disable will show this string and send them looking for a control that is not there. The copy should describe that actual recovery path (or the UI should grow a real regenerate action before the string ships).
